answer: An answer is checkpointed only after a 12-epoch horizon. In that window any peer may post a 6 POA basalt challenge bond and publish proof that two addresses share an operator, for example a reused VRF key-image. If the proof verifies, both identities are voided and the accuser is paid a 12 POA bounty taken from the 20 POA anchor each address locked at registration. A false challenge burns the 6 POA bond. A 40-head farm that recycles one key is therefore publicly challengeable at a profit, so the rational policy is one address per operator.
